summary: The study uses LiF/HCl-etched Ti3C2Tx and compares 15 fabricated electrode materials: a pristine MXene film, four pure hydrazine-foamed MXene variants (MH1-20), five unfoamed Ti3C2Tx/PVA films (MP1-20), and five hydrazine-foamed Ti3C2Tx/PVA composites (MPH1-20). The primary sample, MPH10, is a 10 wt% PVA composite foam made with 5 mL cm−2 hydrazine; in the PVA/H2SO4 gel-electrolyte flexible device it reaches 240.77 F g−1, 264.84 mF cm−2, and 44.06 F cm−3 at 2 mV s−1. Its separately reported conventional-cell value is 237.40 F g−1, 261.14 mF cm−2, and 43.44 F cm−3 at 5 mV s−1 in 1 M H2SO4. Numerical capacitances for the remaining variants are presented only graphically in the supplied main text/SI figure references, so they are not transcribed or estimated here.
